To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
teleoperation and cognitive HRI are complementary.
the usability of teleoperation/telepresences systems can be enhanced by using a set of enhancement-level interfaces.

teleoperation/telepresent interfaces are more suitable for the execution of simple tasks in structured environments, whereas the cognitive HRI is more appropriate for the performance of complex tasks in unstructured environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a human-robot interface for a service robot that will be capable of performing complex tasks in an open environment.
human factors in human-robot interaction.
the usability and cognitive aspects of teleoperation and HRI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cognitive interface is a promising concept for the future HRI.
the human service robot interface is a very complex system, where the usability aspects are very important and the development is still in the very early stage.
telepresence is not a substitute for direct interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to create a human-robot interface that enables a robot to perform complex tasks in a natural way.
the cognitive human-robot interface is a key element of a service robot.
the development of a cognitive HRI is not an easy task, since it involves a number of different disciplines and requires a lot of effort and time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HRI is not just about the user interface but about the whole interaction between a human and a robot.
a cognitive interface should provide the user with the possibility to interact with the robot on a higher cognitive level.
the HRI is the bottleneck for the successful introduction of FSRs.
